claims.claim: For the source-literal optimized FIFO algorithm, every actual queue Q_t is duplicate-free and has exactly the current descent bottoms; processing (p_t,Q_t) yields p_{t+1}=reverse(Q_t) followed by the stable deletion of Q_t from p_t, and the complexity is Θ(n+M_FIFO), where M_FIFO=Σ_t|Q_t|.
claims.evidence: Initialization queues every descent bottom exactly once. Moving distinct q_1,…,q_r successively to the front gives q_r,…,q_1 followed by the unmoved subsequence. Descents inside that reversed prefix are detected exactly by the front test. For an unmoved successor, a consecutive block of old descent bottoms is decreasing; as its members are deleted, the successor can cross from ascent to descent only once, exactly when x<Next(x)<Prev(x), so the deletion test detects it once and creates no duplicate. Initialization costs Θ(n), every queue item costs Θ(1), and every nonempty round processes at least one item, yielding Θ(n+M_FIFO).
claims.witness: All 409,113 permutations through n=9 satisfied queue/descent equality, duplicate-freedom, the stated round transformation, and sorted termination. All 1,240,498 choices of a permutation and arbitrary ordering of its descent-bottom set through n=8 also satisfied the next-queue invariant.
claims.search_method: General local-adjacency case analysis, exhaustive permutation enumeration, arbitrary queue-order enumeration, and independent direct-vector/linked-list execution comparison.

claims.claim: There is an exact phase decomposition: if i is the largest unfixed value and starts its phase at position s_i, that phase makes exactly (i−s_i)+Σ_tℓ_t moves, where ℓ_t counts its round-t queued elements initially left of i.
claims.evidence: Values larger than i form a fixed suffix, so i lies at s_i<i, is not queued, and has a smaller right neighbor until fixation. In a round, moving an element initially left of i shifts i left on deletion and right on prepending, for net zero; moving one initially right shifts i right exactly once. If q_t is the number on the right, the round has ℓ_t+q_t moves and advances i by q_t. Summing q_t=i−s_i proves the identity, including the final round.
claims.witness: The identity was checked phase-by-phase on every permutation of sizes 1 through 9, with ℓ_t computed from each round-start shelf.
claims.search_method: Exact position-shift accounting followed by exhaustive phase decomposition over 409,113 permutations.

claims.claim: For every k≥1, the permutation A_k=(k+1,1,k+2,2,…,2k,k,3k+1,2k+1,2k+2,…,3k) has initial FIFO queue Q_0=(1,2,…,k,2k+1).
claims.evidence: Each low j is immediately preceded by k+j and is therefore a descent bottom. Boundaries from j to k+j+1 are ascents, k to 3k+1 is an ascent, 2k+1 is the sole descent bottom after 3k+1, and the remaining tail is increasing. Thus the scan queues exactly the claimed sequence.
claims.witness: For k=3, A_3=(4,1,5,2,6,3,10,7,8,9) and the exact initial queue is (1,2,3,7). Checks passed for every k≤250.
claims.search_method: Symbolic examination of every adjacent-pair type, supplemented by exact construction checks.

claims.claim: Writing a=3k+1 and c_t=2k+1+t, the actual detection-ordered queue in round t of A_k begins (1,2,…,k−t,c_t) for every 0≤t<k.
claims.evidence: The initial case follows from claim 2. Inductively, Prev(j)=j+1 for displayed lows at the next round start. Processing 1 produces no event; for j≥2, the preceding processed j−1 is the front and is appended by the front test, while the deletion test would require an integer strictly between j and j+1 and is impossible. In round 0 the larger separators similarly make deletion tests false. The still-adjacent a,c_t,c_{t+1} triple then appends c_{t+1} through the deletion test before the front event or any undisplayed queue item. This proves the ordered prefix for all required t.
claims.witness: For k=3, the first queues are Q_0=(1,2,3,7), Q_1=(1,2,8,3), and Q_2=(1,9,2,4), exhibiting the claimed prefixes. Exact checks passed for k≤250.
claims.search_method: Induction following the source's precise deletion-test/front-test/move event order, plus finite exact traces.

claims.claim: Let R(n) be the maximum, over source-literal executions on n values and over ordered adjacent inversion pairs (y,x), of the number of moves of x made while Prev(x)=y. Then R(n)≥⌊(n−1)/3⌋−1 for n≥4, and hence R(n)=Ω(n). Therefore a charging proof that charges every move to its actual predecessor–descent-bottom pair cannot impose a uniform O(1) capacity per pair.
claims.evidence: For A_k, rounds t=1,…,k−1 begin their queues with 1 and have Prev(1)=2. Because 1 is processed first, each round contributes another move charged to the same inversion (2,1). Appending the at-most-two larger ranks needed to reach arbitrary n leaves these transitions unchanged. Taking k=⌊(n−1)/3⌋ gives the bound and rules out constant capacity for this prescribed actual-pair charging rule.
claims.witness: The repeated first-queue event Q_t[0]=1 with Prev_t(1)=2 was checked for every k≤250 and every 1≤t<k.
claims.search_method: Deduction from the proved queue-prefix invariant, fixed-suffix extension, and exact trace validation.

claims.claim: If W(n) is the worst-case source-literal move count, then W(n)≥(k²+3k)/2 for k=⌊(n−1)/3⌋; in particular W(n)=Ω(n²), improving the source lower bound for the optimized algorithm.
claims.evidence: Claim 3 gives at least k−t+1 queued moves in each round t=0,…,k−1. Their exact sum is (k+1)+k+⋯+2=(k²+3k)/2. For general n, appending ranks 3k+2,…,n as an increasing larger suffix neither queues them nor changes the first k transitions. Since k=n/3+O(1), this is an Ω(n²) move and step lower bound.
claims.witness: For k=100 (n=301), the certified first-k-round bound is 5,150 moves; the exact complete execution made 165,358 moves. The bound also survived zero-, one-, and two-element fixed-suffix extensions in the checker.
claims.search_method: Exact summation of the universal queue-prefix lower bound, with construction and suffix-extension checks.

claims.claim: The audited ordinary-transition staircase argument remains invalid for literal FIFO; the new Ω(n²) lower bound is independent of it.
claims.evidence: The ordinary transition processes current descent bottoms in shelf order, whereas subsequent literal queues use event-detection order. These orders produce different states on the stated six-element instance, invalidating transfer of the ordinary recurrence to literal FIFO. The A_k proof instead follows literal FIFO events directly and does not invoke that recurrence.
claims.witness: Starting from (6,1,2,3,4,5), three ordinary transitions yield (3,1,2,6,4,5), while three literal FIFO rounds yield (1,3,2,6,4,5).
claims.search_method: Direct exact evaluation of both transition definitions for the supplied distinguishing instance, followed by a dependency check of the A_k proof.

claims.claim: For n≤9, the exact maximum source-literal move counts remain 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53.
claims.evidence: Exhaustive lexicographic enumeration of all Σ_{n=1}^9 n!=409,113 permutations reproduced exactly the listed maxima. A direct-vector implementation simultaneously checked the queue invariants, while an independently structured array-backed linked-list transcription agreed on every permutation's move and round counts.
claims.witness: One reproduced maximizer at n=9 is (9,1,6,3,2,7,4,8,5), with 53 moves; the complete maxima output is 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53.
claims.search_method: Complete finite search over every permutation for n=1,…,9 with two independently structured literal transcriptions.

claims.claim: A twice-per-unordered-pair charging bound remains false.
claims.evidence: A bound allowing at most two charges per unordered pair would imply M≤2·binom(n,2). Exact literal execution of the supplied n=4096 permutation makes 49,545,006 moves, strictly exceeding 16,773,120. This is a concrete counterexample to that charging bound.
claims.search_method: O(n+M) exact array-backed linked-list execution, cross-validated against the direct transcription on every permutation through n=9.

claims.claim: The requested asymptotically tight worst-case complexity remains unresolved, but the proved interval for the source-literal optimized FIFO algorithm is now Ω(n²)–O(n³).
claims.evidence: Claim 5 rigorously supplies Ω(n²), and claim 0 transfers the move bound to steps. The source supplies O(n³); independently, during active phase i there are at most i−1 rounds and O(i) moves per round, whose sum over i is O(n³). No argument in the draft controls the left-of-active phase term sufficiently for O(n²), nor proves a superquadratic lower bound. Thus the interval is valid but non-tight.
claims.witness: The established endpoints are the A_k lower bound (1/18+o(1))n² and the phase/source O(n³) upper bound; no matching endpoint appears in the draft.
claims.search_method: Dependency audit of the lower and upper bounds and adversarial search for an unstated matching argument or invalid inference.

target_evidence: The target requests an asymptotically tight worst-case complexity. The draft rigorously improves the source-literal optimized FIFO lower bound from Ω(n log n) to Ω(n²), but retains the O(n³) upper bound and explicitly does not claim tightness. This is material, correct partial progress rather than a complete resolution.
